types.embedding_query_text: Technology: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes. Also called tech, innovation. Examples: AI, artificial intelligence, machine learning.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: AI is a technology, best represented as a SoftwareApplication.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

types.embedding_query_text: Shelfmark Examples: Borg.lat.898.

chosen_type.label: Shelfmark
chosen_type.definition: A unique identifier assigned to a manuscript or archival item, typically indicating its location in a collection.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits a shelfmark; minting a new type.

candidates.label: BookmarkAction
candidates.comment: A BookmarkAction is an OrganizeAction where an agent marks an object for later retrieval or reference. Also called flag action, tag action, label action, mark action. Examples: saving a webpage to favorites, tagging an email, marking a chapter in an e-book.

candidates.label: BreadcrumbList
candidates.comment: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: OfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An OfferCatalog is an ItemList containing related Offers and/or further OfferCatalogs from the same provider. Also called product catalog, service catalog, sales brochure. Examples: an online store's product categories, a printed catalog of items for sale, a menu of services. Distinct from ItemList, which is a general list of items.
